correctness.rationale: Two area elements and the sixth distance power scale by length to the tenth power, canceled by area to the fifth power. The oblique-coordinate change contributes (2/sqrt(3))^3. I reconstructed the quartic-and-higher moment calculation independently using Green's theorem: M_pq=(p+1)^(-1) ∮u^(p+1)v^q dv, evaluated along straight edges. Near the given ordered vertices these are the actual convex polygon moments; their polynomial extensions can be evaluated at interpolation nodes even outside that neighborhood. The area polynomial has degree at most two and the energy degree at most ten. Exact interpolation on eleven nodes gives their first and second directional derivatives, and polarization gives all mixed entries. It verifies area 3 and energy 5157/280 in oblique coordinates, the Euclidean normalized value 191 sqrt(3)/2835, vanishing log gradient, and every supplied entry and all four characteristic quadratics of the log-Hessian. The matrix is real symmetric and each quadratic has positive sum and product of roots, so the eight nonzero modes are positive. Similarity invariance and stationarity put the two translation, scale and rotation tangents in the kernel, hence exhaust it. Fixing the first two vertices by the unique nearby direct similarity gives an explicit smooth transverse slice; local convexity and orientation are open, and Taylor's theorem gives strict minimality on that slice and exactly the stated equality cases.
residual_risks: The strict conclusion is local among cyclically labeled positively oriented convex hexagons, not global or uniform across exponents. The verification is exact arithmetic, not proof-assistant or expert attestation.

value.rationale: The sixth power is the first even case beyond the known second- and fourth-power global inequalities. The cited numerical work directly motivates determining whether regular hexagons are stable under arbitrary nearby vertex perturbations. The exact full transverse Hessian answers that question rigorously and separates actual shape directions from the four similarity directions. Its value is the strict local theorem in nonaffine directions, not the length of the characteristic polynomial or the numerical value by itself.
residual_risks: No global polygonal isoperimetric minimization, crossing exponent, or statement at other orders is proved by this review.
